sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Chatha is a qualified food-service supplier entering a much larger capacity phase, not yet a proven high-return compounder. Parent FY26 sales grew only 5.49% to ₹165.80 crore, while parent cash capex and JV equity consumed much more than operating cash. July commissioning is a real milestone; customer acceptance, utilisation and parent funding now determine returns. Supported quality scores remain available, but IAS is NS because full-group economics and funding are conditional. This is a research hold, not a purchase recommendation.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Chatha Foods Limited, ISIN INE0AH901011, BSE SME 544151, listed 27 March 2024. Review cutoff is 20 October 2026. The ₹83.95 observation is a secondary 19 October close, not a live quote. All 119,000 warrants have converted, giving 24,200,879 shares; no remaining warrant proceeds are assumed. One lot is 1,000 shares. Parent Accounting Standards statements are the growth baseline; the first FY26 group includes Allana, whose stake subsequently changed. Financial-history confidence is medium, while the full-group forward valuation is low. G1–G4 remain Conditional.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 5, MOAT 6, REV 7, DUR 7, CAP 4, CASH 5, BAL 5, EXEC 5 and EARN 6 are supported judgments with counterevidence. BQS is 5.52 and Growth Quality GQS 6.20. R is NS; D 4, P 5 and L 5 remain separately scoreable. Original weights, coverage and exact bounds are retained without reweighting. No persistent low-CAP/CASH override is imposed. Missing full-group valuation inputs do not erase the comparable parent record.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company manufactures frozen processed meat, vegetarian and ready-to-cook foods for QSR, institutional and food-service customers. Food safety, product qualification, cold-chain integrity and recipe consistency are central to customer retention. FY26 remained overwhelmingly non-vegetarian; the new 16,000 MT vegetarian plant broadens categories. The Allana partnership offers another production and market-access route, but partner assets, capital and sales are not wholly owned parent economics. Facility capacity is not equivalent to contracted demand or interchangeable product output.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Established QSR relationships and qualification requirements create moderate switching friction. Concentrated buyers can nevertheless multi-source and negotiate prices; management acknowledges top-four concentration as a key risk. Venky’s primary FY26 statements show ₹3,727.32 crore sales, ₹139.25 crore PAT, ₹191.32 crore CFO and ₹41.13 crore cash capex. Its broader poultry, animal-health and oilseed mix, scale and Ind AS accounting make it an economic comparator rather than an identical valuation peer. No peer P/E is imported. Chatha must demonstrate that new vegetarian products earn acceptable margins after distribution and start-up costs.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Constant-parent operating sales were ₹61.1806/₹87.3341/₹117.2277/₹133.7993/₹157.1659/₹165.7966 crore in FY21–26. Five-year CAGR is 22.07%, but the three-year rate is 12.25% and latest growth only 5.49%. REV 7 therefore adjusts the five-year band down one point rather than presenting a pandemic rebound as unchanged momentum. PAT moved from a ₹4.0035 crore FY21 loss to ₹6.6955 crore in FY26. The prospectus reconciliation reports no material profit/equity restatement adjustments. First-group sales of ₹165.7233 crore reflect eliminations, not a new acquired growth engine.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: FY26 parent cash capex was ₹21.3024 crore after capital-advance and creditor offsets, with a separate ₹18.90 crore JV equity investment. Group cash capex was ₹56.0982 crore; the parent investment is not added again to group capex. The vegetarian facility began commercial production on 27 July; the 9 July JV notice described readiness and ongoing customer audits. September management targets 30,800 MT capacity by FY28, about 75% utilisation and ₹550 crore group revenue by FY29. These are ambitions, not verified orders. Existing CWIP and paid advances are not paid twice in the model, and the original commitment-note layout is not treated as a new ₹3.2153 crore unpaid bill.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Three executive directors received ₹1.56 crore combined, versus about ₹0.84 crore previously, materially faster growth than profit. Expense reimbursements are separate. Parent guarantees comprise ₹15 crore term-loan and ₹5 crore working-capital support for Allana. The August agreement changes parent ownership from 70% to 51%, with each partner nominating two directors and partner funding through equity and CCPS; economic rights require more than multiplying group profit by 51%. The ₹40 crore related-party authority is a ceiling, not actual spending. Statutory opinion is unmodified, but that does not independently validate all new-project returns. Small ordinary tax and provident-fund disclosures do not establish misconduct.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Parent FY26 CFO of ₹10.0962 crore improved from negative ₹1.0721 crore; FY24–26 cumulative CFO/PAT is about 66%. Parent FCF after cash capex is negative ₹11.2062 crore, while group FCF is negative ₹46.0963 crore. The ₹19.3514 crore bank-deposit release is investing cash, not operating earnings. True parent cash is ₹4.3251 crore; ₹0.224 crore deposits are restricted. Gross debt is ₹25.7671 crore, already including ₹3.4983 crore current maturities. Core EBITDA reconstructs to ₹12.5756 crore; removing a ₹0.1156 crore prior-tax release and tax-effected other income gives an illustrative ₹6.3146 crore normalized PAT proxy. Receivables fell to ₹21.6297 crore, but ₹0.4865 crore is over one year old. Borrowing-cost capitalisation and commissioning can change future interest/depreciation burdens; current coverage is not extrapolated unchanged.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At the dated quote, equity value is about ₹203.17 crore, around 30.3× parent reported earnings. The parent-only funded model assumes bear/base/bull sales growth 5%/18%/30%, EBITDA margins 7%/10%/12%, NWC 20%/16%/14% and exit multiples 7/10/13. It pays existing capital creditors, known ₹1.40 crore subsequent JV contributions, new completion spending and maintenance, and includes only the actual ₹1.1335 crore remaining warrant cash once. New draws carry half-year interest, jointly solved with tax; repayments occur at year-end. Conditional bear/base/bull terminal prices ₹30.72/₹155.65/₹407.18 imply annual returns -18.21%/13.14%/37.14%. Main cases exclude all JV terminal value and earnings, with recovery sensitivities shown separately. This conservative parent scope is not a full-group fair value, so R remains NS. The model pays the separately excluded ₹0.1527 crore opening net tax payable once in FY27. The ₹0.0737 crore tax refund remains excluded because its recovery/set-off timing is unverified. The opening-claim bridge also pays ₹1.222400 crore of excluded current employee/interest claims once in FY27, and retains ₹2.231700 crore of net noncurrent employee/deposit claims as a terminal equity deduction. It does not force noncurrent claims into immediate repayment. Future operating compensation is cash funded with the opening net deficit held constant; existing taxes, capital creditors and normal WC liabilities are not charged twice.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Major customers can slow ordering or resist raw-material price pass-through as new plants add fixed costs. Cold-chain or food-safety failures can disrupt supply. A slow vegetarian/JV ramp can consume working capital before assets earn returns, while parent guarantees transmit JV stress. The severe model combines falling sales, 4% margin, 28% NWC, 15% funding cost, additional JV support and the full ₹20 crore guarantee call. It is a stress, not a predicted default. FY26’s small TDS/PF balances and the old GST amount reported paid but still shown on the portal are not inflated into an integrity allegation. Positive current CFO and equity are real counterweights. With all identified opening claims included, severe peak required debt is ₹156.0750 crore and terminal price is ₹0.0000; these are conditional requirements, not committed facilities.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold current equity values are approximately ₹1,016 crore and ₹2,032 crore. At an illustrative 20× P/E and 8% net margin, they require roughly ₹635 crore and ₹1,270 crore annual sales before debt, cash and minority adjustments. Management’s ₹550 crore group ambition is not equivalent to parent earnings or proof of that valuation. Partner ownership, CCPS rights, new working capital and possible future dilution can absorb business growth before it reaches each listed share. The conditional bull case does not establish a tenfold thesis.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track customer acceptance, billed volumes, realised margins and utilisation at the vegetarian and JV plants separately. Reconcile remaining completion invoices, opening capital creditors, borrowing capitalisation and post-commissioning depreciation. Obtain JV equity/CCPS terms, governance rights, funding budgets and guarantee release conditions. Check actual post-March cash deployment; all IPO and received preferential proceeds were reported utilised by March. For liquidity, 60 matched secondary observations give mean/median low×volume ₹20.80/₹13.38 lakh and a conditional ₹5 lakh exit of 7.47 sessions at 5% participation. The ₹83,950 lot cost does not establish live depth; no BSE surveillance clearance is inferred.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed deep conditional hold. Established manufacturing capability, a six-year parent history and positive recent operating cash support some quality, but new-capacity returns, concentrated buyers and group funding prevent a high-conviction compounder classification. IAS is NS because material full-group expected-return inputs remain unresolved, not because annual funding work is omitted. Reconsider after operating ramp, cash conversion, economic ownership and funding are independently evidenced. No personal allocation or trade instruction is made.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The primary record includes the final IPO prospectus, FY24 and FY26 annual reports, actual warrant conversion and trading approvals, July commercial/readiness notices, August JV agreement and September AGM transcript. The original capital-commitment layout was visually checked before interpreting cash requirements. Venky’s primary statements provide a bounded economic comparison. The linked model includes five annual operating and funding rows, interest/tax circularity, terminal-equity bridges and margin, WC, capex, JV support, guarantee, dilution and recovery tests. Remaining gaps concern actual interim cash, JV rights and performance, uncommitted headroom and live execution; no missing item is represented as verified. Opening claims are reconciled separately: current exclusions settle once, normal operating balances remain in WC, and net noncurrent employee/deposit claims reduce terminal equity without an unsupported immediate-payout assumption.

GOV.reason: Named bank guarantees and material JV authority require oversight; executive pay rose much faster than profit. Contrary evidence: unmodified audit, disclosed transaction terms and no material prospectus profit restatement. Ordinary paid/disputed tax entries are not misconduct.

MOAT.reason: Food-safety qualification, established QSR relationships and new dedicated facilities support capability. Contrary evidence: concentrated buyers, multi-sourcing and the distinction between commissioning and accepted customer demand limit pricing power.

REV.reason: Five-year constant-parent CAGR 22.07% maps to 8, adjusted down one point for the pandemic-low starting base, three-year CAGR 12.25% and latest 5.49% growth. The full older series is used; the new JV does not inflate it. New facilities are upside counterevidence, not already earned growth.

DUR.reason: Convenience food and food-service customer expansion offer a multi-year runway; vegetarian capacity broadens categories. Concentration, cold-chain risks and customer audits can interrupt it. Management’s ₹550 crore ambition is not an order book.

CAP.reason: Parent cash capex 21.30 and JV investment 18.90 were large versus 6.70 profit; March CWIP is 40.60. Returns on new assets remain unproved. Contrary evidence: July commercial start and positive current CFO mean this is not proof of waste.

CASH.reason: FY26 CFO improved to 10.10 from negative 1.07, but three-year conversion is about 66% and current parent FCF is negative 11.21. Receivables declined and deposits were released, providing counterweights. No persistent low-CASH cap is imposed.

BAL.reason: Parent gross debt 25.77 exceeds true cash 4.33; guarantees add 20 of contingent JV exposure. Group debt is 40.77 and is not confused with parent debt. Equity 89.24 and lower receivables are offsets, but unused sanctioned headroom is unverified.

EXEC.reason: The vegetarian facility has a dated commercial-start notice and the JV completed commissioning. Earlier export/start ambitions preceded the eventual customer-audit ramp. New management capacity and utilisation are unproved; commissioning is meaningful counterevidence.

EARN.reason: Parent profit is positive across FY22–26 and other income is only 0.35; core EBITDA reconstructs to 12.58. Prior-tax release 0.12 and depreciation/interest after commissioning complicate extrapolation; pandemic losses and the new JV are retained.

R.reason: Annual funded scenarios are complete, but JV economic/CCPS rights, future parent support, completion cash and new-facility asset lives prevent a supported full-group expected-return score. Parent-only base IRR is conditional, not adopted as fair value.

D.reason: Strong equity and tangible operating assets provide some buffer; parent guarantees, concentrated demand and the severe funded loss path weaken permanent-loss protection. No guarantee call is asserted as probable.

P.reason: Current capacity and dated commissioning support a credible ramp route, but July start does not verify sales utilisation or the ambitious group target. Base probability is not estimated from management optimism alone.

L.reason: All 60 dated secondary observations are present; conservative low×volume implies 7.47 sessions for a ₹5 lakh exit at 5% participation, within the 5–10 day band. A ₹83,950 lot is manageable at that reference size. Secondary history, price limits and no live depth remain counterevidence; no zero fill or surveillance clearance is inferred.

gates.reason: JV guarantees, equal board rights and rising executive compensation require monitoring. No independently established disqualifying integrity finding; ordinary tax entries are not misconduct.

Audited parent history and actual share conversions are usable. New-group economics, remaining cash commitments and post-commissioning depreciation are conditional, not a blanket critical reliability failure.

Linked annual models explicitly fund new spending, old capital creditors, JV contributions and scheduled repayments. Stress draws are requirements, not sanctioned facilities; unfinanceability is not proved.
Dated secondary trades and lot size support a conditional L score. No live execution or blanket surveillance clearance is established, but effective untradeability is not proved.

EBITDA less estimated depreciation and solved interest gives taxable profit; tax is 25% on positive amounts. Known JV contributions of 1.4 are paid in FY27; future support and guarantees are separate stresses. Scheduled principal of 3.4983 per year is a simplified runoff assumption; additional refinancing is explicitly drawn. Opening debt bears a full year and new borrowing half a year of interest; interest, tax and funding are solved jointly. Ordinary and scheduled repayments occur at year-end. Cash floor is 1. Terminal equity equals parent EBITDA times multiple, less parent debt plus free cash, with zero JV value in main cases. Parent guarantees are not deducted alongside JV debt: the parent-only model does not include JV debt, and stress calls are explicit. Terminal JV book-value sensitivities are illustrative recoveries, not verified fair values. IRR=(terminal price/83.95)^0.2−1. Opening-claim extension: first-year CFO includes the separately settled opening tax and excluded current employee/interest claims. Previously accrued taxes and capital creditors are not paid twice. Old unpaid dividends are financing cash outflows without new buyer entitlement. Net noncurrent employee/deposit claims reduce terminal equity once, while normal WC liabilities remain within the operating cash bridge.
